FIGlet - Frank, Ian & Glenn's Letters
======================================

FIGlet is a program that creates large characters out of ordinary screen characters.

Example:

 _ _ _          _   _     _       
| (_) | _____  | |_| |__ (_)___   
| | | |/ / _ \ | __| '_ \| / __|  
| | |   <  __/ | |_| | | | \__ \_ 
|_|_|_|\_\___|  \__|_| |_|_|___(_)

FIGlet can create characters in many different styles and can kern and "smush" 
these characters together in various ways. FIGlet output is generally reminiscent 
of the sort of "signatures" many people like to put at the end of e-mail and 
UseNet messages.

Official FIGlet web page: http://www.figlet.org/
Contact: info@figlet.org


Usage
-----

Basic usage:
    figlet [options] [message]

If no message is provided, FIGlet reads from standard input.

Examples:
    figlet Hello, world!
    echo "Hello, world!" | figlet
    figlet -f banner "Hello"


Command Line Options
--------------------

Font and Layout:
    -f <fontfile>       Use the specified font
    -d <fontdir>        Specify directory for fonts
    -c                  Center the output
    -l                  Left-align the output (default)
    -r                  Right-align the output
    -k                  Use kerning (reduce spacing between characters)
    -W                  Full-width mode (no character smushing)
    -o                  Overlap mode
    -m <mode>           Specify layout mode

Text Direction:
    -L                  Left-to-right text (default)
    -R                  Right-to-left text

Output Control:
    -w <width>          Specify output width
    -t                  Use terminal width for output
    -p                  Paragraph mode (for multi-line input)

Control Files:
    -C <controlfile>    Use specified control file
    -N                  Clear control file list

Information:
    -I <infocode>       Print information about FIGlet
                        -I 0: version and license
                        -I 1: version
                        -I 2: default font directory
                        -I 3: default font
                        -I 4: output width
                        -I 5: supported font formats
    -v                  Print version information

Other:
    -s                  Smushing mode (default)
    -S                  Use old smushing rules
    -n                  Normal mode (no smushing)
    -D                  Use Deutsch (German) layout rules
    -E                  Use English layout rules (default)
    -X                  Use default layout rules
    -x                  Disable smushing override


Available Fonts
---------------

FIGlet comes with numerous fonts stored in the fonts/ directory.
Font files have the extension .flf (FIGlet font) or .flc (FIGlet control file).

Standard fonts include:
    - banner      - Big banner-style letters
    - big         - Large letters
    - block       - Solid block letters  
    - bubble      - Bubble-style letters
    - digital     - Digital display style
    - ivrit       - Hebrew (right-to-left)
    - lean        - Lean letters
    - mini        - Tiny letters
    - script      - Script style
    - shadow      - Letters with shadow
    - slant       - Slanted letters
    - small       - Small letters
    - standard    - Standard font (default)
    - term        - Terminal-style letters

And many more fonts and control files for various character sets and languages.


Mailing Lists
-------------

FIGlet mailing lists:
    figlet@figlet.org           - General discussion
    figletfonts@figlet.org      - Font announcements
    figletsoftware@figlet.org   - Software announcements

Subscribe at: http://www.figlet.org/mailman/listinfo/


Additional Resources
--------------------

More fonts available at: http://www.figlet.org/
FTP site: ftp://ftp.figlet.org/pub/figlet/


Authors
-------

FIGlet was written by Glenn Chappell and Ian Chai.
Current maintainer: Claudio Matsuoka <cmatsuoka@gmail.com>
Project coordination: Christiaan Keet <info@figlet.org>

.SH DESCRIPTION
.B FIGlet
prints its input using large characters
(called ``FIGcharacters'')made up of ordinary
screen characters
(called ``sub-characters'').
.B FIGlet
output is generally reminiscent of the
sort of ``signatures'' many people like to put at the end of e-mail
and UseNet messages.  It is also reminiscent of the output of some banner
programs, although it is oriented normally, not sideways.

.B FIGlet
can print in a variety of fonts, both left-to-right and right-to-left,
with adjacent FIGcharacters kerned and ``smushed'' together in various ways.
.B FIGlet
fonts are stored in
separate files, which can be identified by the suffix
.RB `` .flf ''.
In systems with UTF-8 support
.B FIGlet
may also support TOIlet
.RB `` .tlf ''
fonts.  Most
.B FIGlet
font files will be stored in
.B FIGlet's
default font directory.

.B FIGlet
can also use ``control files'', which tell it to map certain input
characters to certain other characters, similar to the Unix
.B tr
command.  Control files can be identified by the suffix
.RB `` .flc ''.
Most
.B FIGlet
control files will be stored in
.B FIGlet's
default font directory.

You can store
.B FIGlet
fonts and control files
in compressed form.

.SH ORIGIN
.RB `` FIGlet ''
stands for ``Frank, Ian and Glenn's LETters''.  Inspired by Frank's .sig,
Glenn wrote (most of) it, and Ian helped.

Most of the standard
.B FIGlet
fonts were inspired by signatures on various UseNet
articles.  Since typically hundreds of people use the same style of
letters in their signatures, it was often not deemed necessary to give
credit to any one font designer.

.SH BUGS
Very little error checking is done on font and control files.  While
.B FIGlet
tries to be forgiving of errors, and should (hopefully) never actually
crash, using an improperly-formatted file with
.B FIGlet
will produce unpredictable output.

.B FIGlet
does not handle format characters in a very intelligent way.
A tab character is converted to a blank, and vertical-tab, form-feed and
carriage-return are each converted to a newline.  On many systems, tabs
can be handled better by piping files through
.B expand
before piping through
.BR FIGlet .

.B FIGlet
output is quite ugly if it is displayed in a proportionally-spaced font.
I suppose this is to be expected.

Please report any errors you find in this man page or the program to
<info@figlet.org>

for general discussions about 
.B FIGlet 
and a place where you can ask questions or share ideas 
with other 
.B FIGlet

news about new fonts, new software updates etc.

To subscribe or unsubscribe from the

has an inverse, so that, for example, if
.B FIGlet

.BR alias ,

.B FIGlet
looks for the file first in the default font directory and then
in the current directory, or, if
.I fontfile

.B \-f

.B FIGlet
uses the font that was specified

.PD 0

.B \-X
.PD

.B \-X
(default) makes

use whichever is specified in the font file.

Once the options are read,
if there are any remaining words on the command line,
they are used instead

This feature
allows shell scripts to generate large letters without having to dummy

An empty argument, obtained by two sequential quotes,

.SH EXAMPLES
To use
.B FIGlet
with its default settings, simply type
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet

.ft R
.fi
.RE
and then type whatever you like.

To change the font, use the
.B \-f
option, for example,
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-f script

.ft R
.fi
.RE

Use the
.B \-c
option if you would prefer centered output:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-c

.ft R
.fi
.RE

We have found that the most common use of
.B FIGlet
is making up large text to be placed in e-mail messages.  For this
reason,
.B FIGlet
defaults to 80 column output.  If you are using a wider terminal, and
would like
.B FIGlet
to use the full width of your terminal, use the
.B \-t
option:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-t

.ft R
.fi
.RE

If you don't want
.B FIGlet
to smush FIGcharacters into each other, use the
.B \-k
option:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-k

.ft R
.fi
.RE

If
.B figlet

.BR \-p :
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-p < myfile

.ft R
.fi
.RE

.RS

.ft B

example% figlet \-ptk \-f shadow < anotherfile
example% figlet \-cf slant

.ft R
.fi
.RE

Finally, if you want to have
.B FIGlet
take the input from the command
line instead of a file:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet Hello world

.ft R
.fi
.RE

.B lean

.RS
.nf

example% figlet \-f lean | tr ' _/' '/  '
.ft R
.fi
.RE

Similar things can be done with the
.B block
font and many of the other
.B FIGlet
fonts.

using the

If you don't rename the file appropriately,
.B FIGlet
won't be able to find it.

.B FIGlet
does not care what the filename within the
.B .zip
archive is, and will process only the first file.

The
.B .zip
format was chosen because tools to create and manipulate it
are widely available for free
on many platforms.

then exit.  If several of these options are given on the command line, only
the last is executed, and only after
all other command-line options have been dealt with.

.B \-v
prints version and copyright information, as well as a ``Usage: ...''
line.
.B \-I
prints the information corresponding to the given
.I infocode
in a consistent, reliable (i.e., guaranteed to be the same in
future releases) format.
.B \-I
is primarily intended to be used by programs that use
.BR FIGlet .
.I infocode
can be any of the following.
.RS
.TP
.BR -1 " Normal operation (default)."
This
.I infocode
indicates that
.B FIGlet
should operate normally, not giving any informational printout,
printing its input in the selected font.
.TP
.BR 0 " Version and copyright."
This is identical to
.BR \-v .
.TP
.BR 1 " Version (integer)."
This will print the version of your copy of
.B FIGlet
as a decimal integer.  The main version number is multiplied by 10000,
the sub-version number is multiplied by 100, and the sub-sub-version
number is multiplied by 1.  These are added together, and the result is
printed out.  For example,
.B FIGlet
2.2 will print
.RB `` 20200 ''
, version 2.2.1 will print
.RB `` 20201 ''.
Similarly, version 3.7.2 would print
.RB `` 30702 ''.
These numbers are guaranteed to be
ascending, with later versions having higher numbers.  Note that
the first major release of
.BR FIGlet ,
version 2.0, did not have the
.B \-I
option.
.TP
.BR 2 " Default font directory."
This will print the default font directory.  It is affected by the
.B \-d
option.
.TP
.BR 3 " Font."
This will print the name of the font
.B FIGlet
would use.  It is affected by
the
.B \-f
option.
This is not a filename; the
.RB `` .flf ''
suffix is not printed.
.TP
.BR 4 " Output width."
This will print the value
.B FIGlet
would use for
.IR outputwidth ,
the number of columns wide
.B FIGlet
assumes the screen is.
It is affected by the
.B \-w
and
.B \-t
options.
.TP
.BR 5 " Supported font formats."
This will list font formats supported by
.B FIGlet .
Possible formats are
.RB `` flf2 ''
for FIGfont Version 2
.B .flf
files and
.RB `` tlf2 ''
for TOIlet
.B .tlf
files.
.RE
.IP
If
.I infocode
is any other positive value,
.B FIGlet
will simply exit without printing anything.

.TP
.B \-L
.PD 0
.TP
.B \-R
.PD 0
.TP
.B \-X
.PD
These options control whether
.B FIGlet
prints left-to-right or right-to-left.
.B \-L
selects left-to-right printing.
.B \-R
selects right-to-left printing.
.B \-X
(default) makes
.B FIGlet
use whichever is specified in the font file.

Once the options are read,
if there are any remaining words on the command line,
they are used instead
of standard input as the source of text.
This feature
allows shell scripts to generate large letters without having to dummy
up standard input files.

An empty argument, obtained by two sequential quotes,
results in a line break.

.SH EXAMPLES
To use
.B FIGlet
with its default settings, simply type
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet

.ft R
.fi
.RE
and then type whatever you like.

To change the font, use the
.B \-f
option, for example,
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-f script

.ft R
.fi
.RE

Use the
.B \-c
option if you would prefer centered output:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-c

.ft R
.fi
.RE

We have found that the most common use of
.B FIGlet
is making up large text to be placed in e-mail messages.  For this
reason,
.B FIGlet
defaults to 80 column output.  If you are using a wider terminal, and
would like
.B FIGlet
to use the full width of your terminal, use the
.B \-t
option:
.RS
.nf
.ft B

example% figlet \-t

.ft R
.fi
.RE

.B FIGlet
to smush FIGcharacters into each other, use the

import subprocess, os
os.makedirs("/tmp/custom", exist_ok=True)
def make_font(path, glyphs, height=2, hardblank='$', old=15, full=None, extra_header=""):
    # glyphs dict code->list of strings (without endmark)
    lines=[]
    header=f"flf2a{hardblank} {height} 1 10 {old} 0"
    if full is not None:
        header+=f" 0 {full} 0"
    lines.append(header)
    # no comments
    for code in range(32,127):
        g=glyphs.get(code, ["   "]*height)
        assert len(g)==height
        for i,row in enumerate(g):
            end="@@" if i==height-1 else "@"
            lines.append(row+end)
    open(path,'w').write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")

print(EXE)

# multiple entries deflated
with zipfile.ZipFile("/tmp/zt/zmulti.flf","w",compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z: z.writestr("first.txt", simple_font("1")); z.writestr("second.flf", simple_font("2"))

r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-f","/tmp/zt/zsub.flf"], input=b"A\n", capture_output=True, cwd="/tmp")
print("sub",r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)
with zipfile.ZipFile("/tmp/zt/zbad.flf","w",compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z: z.writestr("x", b"notfont")
r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-f","/tmp/zt/zbad.flf"], input=b"A\n", capture_output=True, cwd="/tmp")
print("bad inner",r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)

def spawn(args, cols, stdin_from="pipe", stdout_to="pty"):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, cols, 0,0))
    kw={}

import os
def strip(s):
    s=s.rstrip('\r\n')
    # rstrip whitespace? our inferred: rstrip all whitespace then drop trailing same char repeatedly
    import re
    s2=s.rstrip(' \t\r\n')
    if not s2: return ''
    c=s2[-1]
    while s2 and s2[-1]==c: s2=s2[:-1]
    return s2

for d in ['fonts','assets']:
 for fn in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
  if not fn.endswith(('.flf','.tlf')): continue
  text=open(os.path.join(d,fn),encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read().splitlines()
  hdr=text[0].split()
  try: h=int(hdr[1]); com=int(hdr[5])
  except: continue
  idx=1+com; diffs=0; examples=[]
  total=95+7
  for gi in range(total):
    rows=[strip(x) for x in text[idx:idx+h]]; idx+=h
    if len(set(map(len,rows)))>1:
      diffs+=1
      if len(examples)<2: examples.append(rows)
  if diffs: print(fn,"glyphs diff rows",diffs,examples)

def build(name, header):
 lines=[header]
 for code in range(32,127):
   ch=chr(code)
   glyph=" <"+ch+"> " if code!=32 else "   "

   lines.append("[X]@@")
 open(f"/tmp/custom/{name}.flf","w").write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
# We'll create pair font with header variants using make-like manual
def build_pair(name, header):
 lines=[header]
 for code in range(32,127):
   if code==65: g=" | "
   elif code==66: g=" | "
   else: g="   "
   lines.append(g+"@@")
 open(f"/tmp/custom/{name}.flf","w").write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
def run(name,mode=[]):
 r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-d","/tmp/custom","-f",name]+mode, input=b"AB", capture_output=True); return r.stdout
headers={
 "old15_nofull": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0",
 "old0_nofull": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 0 0",
 "oldneg_nofull": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 -1 0",
 "old15_printdir": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0",
 "old15_full79": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 79", # low byte bit6+rules15 -> kern default expected
 "old15_full143": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 143", # controlled rules15
 "old15_full128": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 128", # universal
 "old15_full64": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 64", # kern
 "old15_full0": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 0", # full
 "old15_full_codetag": "flf2a$ 1 1 10 15 0 0 79 0",
}
for name,h in headers.items():
 build_pair(name,h)
 print(name, "def",run(name), "s",run(name,["-s"]), "S",run(name,["-S"]), "k",run(name,["-k"]))

def differs(args,inp):
    a=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, cwd="/workspace")

        i=0
        while i < len(inp):
            cand=inp[:i]+inp[i+size:]
            if cand and differs(args,cand):
                inp=cand; changed=True
            else:
                i+=size

a=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, cwd="/workspace")

Current status: I have implemented a clean-room reimplementation of the FIGlet 2.2.5 executable (as `figlet.py`), plus a `compile.sh` that builds `./executable` from it and a `.gitignore` excluding build artifacts. The implementation was developed purely by probing the provided binary and reading the bundled documentation:

- Full CLI/getopt behavior (all documented options, `-I` info codes, `-v`, `-t` terminal width via stdin ioctl, `-F` special error, GNU getopt argument permutation and `POSIXLY_CORRECT` handling, program-name handling in messages)
- FIGfont (`.flf`) and TOIlet (`.tlf`) font loading, including search order across the font directory and current directory, suffix stripping, Deutsch fallback glyphs, code-tagged glyphs, the code-0 "missing character" fallback, and compressed (deflated zip) fonts such as `flowerpower`
- Kerning, controlled smushing (rules 1–6), universal smushing/overlap, full-width mode, `-m` layout modes, font-default vs forced (`-S`) layouts, right-to-left rendering, justification and wrapping with word-break rollback
- Input processing: command-line message handling (including empty-argument line breaks), paragraph mode, Deutsch mode, tab/control-character handling, and control files (`.flc`) — translate/freeze commands, range and escape parsing, numeric mapping tables, `g` commands, UTF-8, HZ, and Shift-JIS (`b`/`j`) input modes, plus the default ISO-2022 decoder with character-set designations, locking/single shifts and multibyte sets.

I verified it with an extensive differential test harness against the preserved original binary: thousands of cases (all bundled fonts, many layout/width/justification modes, wrapping, paragraph mode, control-file behavior, encoding sequences, font/control error handling) now pass. The few remaining known discrepancies are limited to garbage artifacts the original produces for malformed fonts containing raw high-bytes in glyph rows (stale-buffer behavior), which is not reproducible meaningful behavior.

The fresh-checkout build simulation also succeeds (`./compile.sh` produces a working `./executable`), and the new/modified source files (`figlet.py`, `compile.sh`, `.gitignore`) are staged, ready to be committed and submitted.
